dramatic_truth: Senna hires Greg as a paid model so she can draw weight transfer rather than merely subtract a leg from an ordinary standing body.
performance: Greg negotiates two working hours and gives embodied feedback without becoming art director; Senna learns the crutches are load path, not accessories.
screenplay: Senna recruits Greg; repeated short holds expose changing hand/shoulder load; committee interruption tests whether Senna answers for him; drawing improves when asymmetry becomes structural.
prose_comparison: Pose repetition is the actual visual-learning mechanism and exposes disability as whole-body geometry.

dramatic_truth: Greg takes Tavi to watch seasonal river kites and functions primarily as lookout rather than expert or collector.
performance: He keeps Tavi behind safe viewing geometry, routes a stranded fish to workers, bounds what he knows about the species, and handles Tavi's loose talk about the oval without panic.
screenplay: Fish migration spectacle; public viewing blocks; worker rescue chain; local river veteran supplies bounded mechanism; Tavi/Naro social boundary around Greg's magic objects.
prose_comparison: The long observation sequence carries caretaking, wonder, local knowledge, and privacy learning; it is not a monster-mechanics dump.

dramatic_truth: Greg uses Three Reeds for a real neighbor problem, but the artifact only helps bound the light-spill problem before an ordinary baking tray becomes the safer sustained solution.
performance: Mevi owns her house constraints, Greg keeps the shade unit physically separate and short-duration, and Naro's curiosity reinforces why custody rules exist.
screenplay: Emberwings cluster at west window; Three Reeds reduces lamp spill; heat limit remains unknown; ordinary tray blocks light more safely; Greg takes artifact home rather than leaving it with children.
prose_comparison: The chapter proves useful magic need not be the final or maximal solution and transfers prior test knowledge into bounded practical use.

dramatic_truth: Vale debt decreases through a bounded service-credit paper job while Greg learns that access to account handling does not make other people's financial lives his information.
performance: He transfers bundles by cover mark/page range, holds mismatches, ignores status pressure from a privileged visitor, and confirms the exact post-job balance.
screenplay: East Annex transfer protocol; several holds; Mistress Ceral meets procedure; service credit posts three principal-equivalent; balance moves 26 to 23 while Greg's cash remains separate.
prose_comparison: Paper rhythm makes debt closure physical and reinforces information boundaries.

dramatic_truth: Lyssa accepts her first larger subcontract with Marra while Greg learns partnership can mean witnessing terms and carrying support without owning the decision.
performance: Lyssa asks Greg to hear/repeat terms; Marra and Lyssa separate client changes, shop errors, and Lyssa errors; Greg leaves once support is no longer needed.
screenplay: Cloth delivery opens offer; first-lot terms bounded at six copper/four days; Greg witnesses; he fetches tools/food; Lyssa tests pace at rear bench and returns tired but not miserable.
prose_comparison: The work detail establishes Lyssa's independent commercial agency and Greg's changing relationship behavior.

dramatic_truth: Greg goes dancing with Lyssa for no productive reason and discovers his current body can participate without recreating first-life movement.
performance: He tests safe rhythm and space, takes rests before pain turns into injury, meets Pera, and stays because he wants to rather than because Lyssa asks.
screenplay: Lantern Court invitation; initial body/crowd anxiety; crude dancing with crutches; rest and return; Pera interaction; closing slow piece becomes shared beat rather than performance.
prose_comparison: The chapter's bodily repetition is recreation, relationship, and identity integration, not downtime to cut.

dramatic_truth: Jori hires Greg to teach route discipline under low light because his everyday crutch movement gives him a useful procedural perspective without making him theatre safety authority.
performance: Greg identifies three different movement habits, teaches start point/next fixed boundary/stop condition, and refuses surprise-obstacle theatrics.
screenplay: Three stagehands demonstrate current habits; lights progressively reduce; props obstruct route references; students practice stopping rather than guessing; Greg discovers he still knows how to instruct.
prose_comparison: Training repetition differentiates learners and turns implicit embodied skill into teachable procedure.

dramatic_truth: At a recovery auction Greg practices personal valuation under real bidding pressure and buys useful mundane carrying gear instead of the magical objects that excite him.
performance: He walks the floor before touching, bids and stops on incomplete draft finder and echo pins, notices expert-market signals, then buys a one-copper porter harness with immediate practical use.
screenplay: Recovery sale inspection; several tempting damaged service goods; Greg loses draft finder at four and echo pins at four; porter harness wins at one; empty fit check establishes constraints.
prose_comparison: The auction is a direct test of capital discipline and market learning; repeated bids are distinct value decisions.

dramatic_truth: The porter harness immediately proves useful carrying Lyssa's completed subcontract, while the return inspection tests whether Lyssa can hold scope when Marra's client changed specifications after cutting.
performance: Greg carries without overoptimizing; Marra accepts Lyssa's finishing, owns eight-wrap rework caused by her missed update, pays six, and makes a separate nine-copper second-lot offer.
screenplay: Cargo walk; first-lot inspection; one Lyssa stitch fix; eight client-spec loop errors assigned to shop; six copper paid; larger second lot offered; Lyssa later prices whether repeating this work is desirable.
prose_comparison: The repeated work terms change process, confidence, and bargaining power rather than replaying the first contract.

dramatic_truth: Hessa advances moving-caster training by adding farther stationary-target distance and visible environmental noise on a practiced but less artificial loop.
performance: Greg must skip wind-noisy passes, accept discarded apparent successes, and remain a student instead of pre-solving Hessa's lesson.
screenplay: Loop familiarization; near baseline; farther target ten counted attempts with two clean-enough results; one wind-noisy movement discarded; Hessa refuses generalized skill claims; Lyssa independently accepts second lot afterward.
prose_comparison: Experimental repetition changes distance/noise while explicitly preserving confounds and is doing scientific-character work.
